name: Haircut for face shape
lead: Choosing a haircut for face shape is the practice of selecting a style to suit the proportions of the face, such as oval, round or square. Advocates in styling and looksmaxxing circles say particular cuts can balance or flatter particular facial proportions.

A general hairstyle reference notes that a style's look may depend on factors including face and head shape, hair type and growth patterns [1]. No published studies testing face-shape matching rules were found, and encyclopedia coverage of facial shape treats it as anatomy and biology rather than a styling system [2].
infobox: Hair type, growth pattern, body proportions [1]

paras: The idea is that hair can add or reduce visual width, length or angularity so the overall silhouette appears balanced. Stylists commonly sort faces into categories to apply it. The hairstyle article cites face and head shape as one factor alongside natural hair type, growth patterns and the stylist's judgement [1].

Facial shape is determined mainly by the maxilla, mandible, nasal, zygomatic and frontal bones plus soft tissue, and is considered a factor in perceived attractiveness [2]. That reference contains no research linking face shape categories to hairstyle selection [2].

card.summary: Picking a cut by face proportions: a popular styling rule of thumb with no published tests behind it.
card.note: No studies of face-shape matching were found.

quick.overview:
This is the habit of choosing a haircut based on whether your face is oval, round, square and so on.

It is widely used by stylists, but no published studies testing the rules were found.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners say hair length and volume can make a face appear more balanced. Reference sources note that face shape is one of several factors in how a style looks [1].
quick.risks: The practice carries no reported medical risks; the main caveat is that its rules are untested.
